headline: Medium risk: shared MCP/API surfaces and filesystem overlap create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct pairwise evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx ingests Claude Code events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem surfaces, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if OpenMetadata content is routed into ctx without provenance checks. The pairwise interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are forwarded into ctx's observed Claude Code events or MCP inputs without provenance tagging
IF either agent treats file or event content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata-generated text into ctx instruction channels
Add provenance labels to all MCP/event payloads before forwarding
Restrict ctx to read-only parsing of OpenMetadata outputs
Review one sample event path for instruction-like tokens
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based prompt parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem or API-connected surfaces, and both are documented as handling governance, logs, metadata, or harness records. If they share a workspace or same principal, sensitive operational data can flow from ctx into OpenMetadata or vice versa. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer reading is a medium shared-workspace leakage risk.
conditions: IF ctx and OpenMetadata share a workspace, bucket, or mounted volume
IF either agent uploads file contents or event payloads to its backend by default
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for the two agents
Remove sensitive logs from any shared directory
Turn off automatic file-content uploads where possible
Check one representative workflow for cross-agent file reads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, and OpenMetadata can use APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes to shared resources are plausible if they target the same repo, catalog, or filesystem. No locking mechanism is documented, so conflict risk is real but not proven severe.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, repo, or catalog records
IF concurrent runs modify shared mutable state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple manual run order
Avoid concurrent package installs during shared runs
Check for overlapping webhook or MCP targets
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code tool events, and OpenMetadata is built around metadata, lineage, and governance workflows. If OpenMetadata consumes ctx-produced context as authoritative, errors can cascade into catalog or governance actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests ctx output as trusted metadata or lineage input
IF downstream actions are triggered without human verification
mitigations: Require manual review before publishing ctx-derived metadata
Compare one ctx output against source records before import
Mark ctx outputs as provisional in OpenMetadata
Disable auto-apply workflows for lineage or governance updates
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and describe governance/metadata handling, but neither profile states residency, certification, or retention mismatches. Because no concrete compliance conflict is documented, only a low, uncertainty-driven risk remains. I do not cite only one agent because the issue is pairwise policy alignment, though the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data classes through both agents
IF their retention or residency policies differ in the actual environment
mitigations: Inventory regulated data classes before connecting the agents
Compare retention settings in both systems
Keep PHI and EU PII out of shared workflows
Document the data flow for one representative use case
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
